title: Late Quaternary megafauna extinction
summary: Between about 132,000 and 1,000 years ago, about half of the world's large-bodied mammal species disappeared. In North America about 60 megafaunal species died out, their last dated occurrences typically falling between about 13,000 and 11,000 years ago, and in South America about 66 over a longer span. One global study found extinction severity strongly tied to where humans and other hominins lived, with at most a weak link to climate. Another notes that the causes are still debated.

importance.justification: The loss of about half of the world's large mammal species changed ecosystems on several continents.

related.because: The extinction of Sahul megafauna around 46,000 years ago formed the earliest continental pulse of the late Quaternary extinction wave.
The terminal Pleistocene extinction in the Americas eliminated dozens of megafaunal genera between 13,800 and 11,400 years ago.
The global dispersal of modern humans out of Africa brought human hunting and ecological pressures to naive fauna across all continents.
